title: He healed a man…
paragraphs:
He healed a man…
and they wanted Him dead.

A miracle happened in plain sight—
and it triggered murder in religious hearts.
Because this story isn’t just about them.

You can be in the right place…
with the wrong heart.

You can sit in a synagogue,
know the Scriptures,
follow the rules,
and still completely miss God.
In Mark 3:1–6, Jesus walks into a synagogue where a man is suffering with a withered hand.
“They watched Jesus closely to see whether He would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.” (Mark 3:2)
They were looking for a mistake.

From loving God
to managing appearances?

From seeking truth
to defending your image?
This is the danger of religious pride.
And then Jesus asks a question that cuts deeper than any blade:
“Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to kill?” (Mark 3:4)

Because pride has no answer
when truth speaks plainly.
Then comes one of the most overlooked moments in the Gospel:
“He looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart…” (Mark 3:5)
But not the way we are.

You can know Scripture…
and still resist the God of Scripture.

You can defend the Sabbath…
and reject the Lord of the Sabbath.
And pride always disguises itself as control.

Control of behavior.
Control of perception.
Control of who is “in” and who is “out.”
But Jesus is not impressed by controlled religion.
He is moved by surrendered hearts.
But that command is heavier than it sounds.
Because stretching out that hand means:
And here’s where many of us hesitate.

We don’t mind following Jesus…
until He asks us to reveal the very thing we’ve been hiding.

We’d rather look whole
than be made whole.
But the man stretches it out.
Grace just broke into the room.
“The Pharisees went out and immediately held counsel… how to destroy Him.” (Mark 3:6)
Grace exposes that we cannot save ourselves.
This is where the Gospel explodes into clarity.
Because this moment in the synagogue…
Is pointing straight to the cross.
Because our deepest problem isn’t a withered hand.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
Through His death and resurrection, He did what we could never do:
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Because grace doesn’t meet you in perfection.
What “withered hand” are you keeping tucked away…
Because you’re afraid of being seen?
You don’t have to fix it first.
You don’t have to clean yourself up.
What you place in His hands…
Maybe not always the way you expect.
But always completely in His purpose.
